title: Gate the teacher before distilling
text: Play the rollout teacher itself against c2 first: if exact-ish rollout values cannot beat c2, a student of them cannot either
rejected: Start with the student pilot and the controls (imitation, flat MLP) as in the proposal: postponed to save compute

title: Teacher gate 1 lost; keep going with a z-gate and the student
text: Gate 1 (16-32 draws, margin 0.04): 41.5% after 100 games vs c2, overriding 22% of buys on noise (winner's curse). Gate 2 requires a gain of 2 paired SEs at 32 draws. The student run p1 starts at once: averaging unbiased labels across positions removes the per-position noise; its dev match every round is the test
rejected: Stop the experiment: the proposal's rule, but the failure is explained by noise in single-position play, which distillation addresses

title: Student chooses among the teacher's candidates, with c2's preference as input
text: Round 1 student overrode 76% of buys and scored 0.2% at margin 0: it was trained only on the graded candidates (c2's top 5 + PASS) but picked among all legal cards, including ones it never saw labelled. Now it ranks the same candidate set, and each card token carries c2's probability of buying it, so the student starts near c2 and learns corrections
rejected: Wait for more data: would not fix choices outside the labelled set

title: Labels are noise-dominated per position
text: After 2,118 positions the teacher's best is Copper in 24% of positions and the student's outputs are flat (~0.60 everywhere): one label's paired SE (~0.1) is far above typical buy gaps (0.02-0.05). The student needs on the order of 100k+ positions. Switched to a fixed 16 draws (twice the positions per hour; adaptive draws went to close calls, where the choice matters least), rounds of 20,000 positions, dev margins 0.02/0.05/0.10.

title: Gate 2: the z-gated teacher is ahead
text: Teacher on c2 with 32 paired draws, overriding only when the gain beats 2 paired standard errors and 0.02: 61.0% after 50 games against plain c2 (kingdom-block 95% interval 50-72%), overriding 5% of buys. The rollout values carry real signal; noise was the problem in gate 1.

title: Gate 2 passed: the z-gated teacher beats c2
text: Final: 56.2% over 160 games (80 kingdoms, both seats) against plain c2, kingdom-block 95% interval 50.3-61.9%, overriding 4% of buys (32 paired draws, gain > 2 SE and > 0.02). Rollout buy values improve on RL-v3's best. Next: the same teacher against c1 2300; the student must learn to make these overrides without the rollouts.

title: The gated teacher beats both RL-v3 checkpoints
text: Teacher on c2 (32 paired draws, gain > 2 SE and > 0.02) vs c1 2300: 59.4% over 160 games, 95% interval 52.8-65.9%, override 5%. With 56.2% vs c2 2654 it leads both. Confirmation on the reserved kingdom stream (200 kingdoms, both seats, vs c2 then c1) started. Student after round 5 (49.6k labels): dev regret 0.059 vs incumbent 0.047, dev 49.6-51.8%: not there yet.
